name: Secessionism in Western Australia
summary: Western Australian secessionism holds that the state should leave the Australian federation and govern itself, because Canberra and the eastern states are said to neglect WA, take more of its revenue than they return, and impose trade and resource policies that hurt its exporters. It has been a recurring, mostly pragmatic and grievance-driven cause, strongest during the 1930s Depression, and is not tied to a wider left or right programme.
scope: The profile covers the mainstream of the movement across its documented phases: the 1930s Dominion League and the 1933 referendum, the 1970s Westralian Secession Movement, and the modern WAxit Party platform. It excludes the earlier Goldfields 'Auralia' separatism and one-off remarks by individual politicians, and many general-ideology statements are answered by inference because the movement states no wider doctrine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: WAxit would cut the Medicare levy but replace federal programs from WA revenue, so Medicare-style cover is assumed to continue rather than being a stated goal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Early secessionists were export-minded primary producers, but WAxit also backs preference for local manufacturers and public monopolies, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: The WAxit platform says public assets stay in state hands, with no privatisation of natural monopolies and no toll roads.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: WAxit proposes abolishing or reducing capital gains, fringe benefits and stamp duties, which points away from higher taxes on the wealthy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: WAxit wants less red tape for small business but also obligations on mining companies to hire and train locals, so the net direction is mixed.

worker-ownership.rationale: The programme is about independence and state revenue, not employee ownership, and its small-business orientation points away from it.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement worked through rallies, a parliament and a referendum, and the Dominion League sought constitutional redress, not an authoritarian bypass.

state-harmful.rationale: Secessionists want to build a new self-governing state with its own defence force and budget, so they plainly regard government as necessary.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: WAxit proposes a standalone WA Defence Force, but on policing it prefers targeted drug action over simply more officers, so support is modest.

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

decide-locally.rationale: The central grievance is that Canberra decides for WA, and the remedy is for decisions to be taken in Perth; the statement's local level is read here as the state.

rehabilitation.rationale: WAxit emphasises tackling drug supply and mental health but gives no view on prison philosophy.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Aboriginal affairs are mostly absent from the platform beyond mental health, so adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Dominion League appealed to a distinct Western Australian identity and lost liberty, implying valuing a local tradition, though not as a doctrine.

gradual-change.rationale: The campaign worked through petitions, referendum and appeal to the British Parliament, respecting established institutions even while seeking a major change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: WAxit proposes a targeted skilled-migrant program rather than cuts, so it neither reduces nor expands overall numbers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement's aim is to move sovereignty to a smaller body, so pooling power upward runs against its instincts.

free-trade.rationale: Secessionists objected to protectionist tariffs that hurt WA mining and farming exports, and the 1970s movement focused on trade barriers.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military policy is touched only by a WA Defence Force proposal and nothing on intervention.

open-borders.rationale: WAxit wants controlled, skilled-targeted immigration and its own borders, which is inconsistent with open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: WAxit wants WA to lead in renewable manufacturing but also protects the mining economy, so it is split.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement sought independence by referendum and petition, and the League's later call for a unilateral declaration was rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Secessionists relied on public rallies and a popular vote to decide, which favours the public over expert authority.

socialized-markets.rationale: The platform backs public ownership of monopolies but also private small business, so adherents are split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: WAxit wants lower taxes in general; no inheritance tax is proposed.

basic-income.rationale: The platform offers targeted help such as solar assistance and reduced HECS debt, not an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Secessionists complained that federal protective tariffs favoured eastern manufacturers at WA primary producers' expense, though WAxit favours local-manufacturer preference.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No position is stated, but small business and farm interests lean slightly toward it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: WAxit's budget model rests on a taxed money economy and wages.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No hint of state-recognised wage bargaining in the platform.

one-party-rule.rationale: WAxit criticises parties subordinate to national interests and contests elections, so a single guiding party is alien to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The 1933 movement sought dominion status under the Crown, but the modern WAxit party includes republican merger members and states no head-of-state position.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1933 case rested on a popular majority vote, and the movement appeals to democratic consent.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1933 secession referendum shows a preference for deciding the constitutional question directly, though no general doctrine of direct legislation is stated.

workers-councils.rationale: No relation to the movement; it seeks a conventional parliamentary state.

right-to-secede.rationale: The whole movement holds that WA can legitimately leave the federation, contrary to the constitution's description of it as indissoluble.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement was a popular campaign appealing to equal citizens' votes.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement is commercially and fiscally motivated; nothing glorifies war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion plays no role in the programme, so a secular state is the default inference.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nothing in the programme refers to scripture as a basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: WAxit proposes a state-funded WA Defence Force rather than private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: The proposed defence force is sized at WA's share of national defence spending, a modest aim, but nothing addresses superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The programme defines WA by territory and wants skilled migrants, with no ethnic definition.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement frames conflict as state against federation, not class against class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No egalitarian programme appears in the platform; its focus is on opportunity and regional development.

civilizational-union.rationale: Secessionists want to divide a political union, not merge states on civilizational lines.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Grievance about fiscal contribution is interest-based, but no moral doctrine on self-interest appears.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The platform stresses freedom and reduced tax burdens, not duty over rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: WAxit backs renewables but opposes Kimberley parks that limit water development, so adherents are split.

limit-population.rationale: WAxit explicitly wants families supported to have more children and a skilled-immigration program.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The platform supports mining, manufacturing and heavy rail, which is opposed to this view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: High-tech industry is backed, but nothing endorses disruption of institutions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is absent from the WAxit platform and from the historical campaigns, so adherents are simply split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The 1933 question was framed as return to a self-governing colony, but nothing in the sources makes restoration outweigh progress.

direct-action.rationale: Secessionists used elections, referendums and petitions rather than direct action.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: WAxit wants specialised regional industry and added-value processing.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A budget-surplus model funding infrastructure and debt retirement, not need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: WAxit focuses on mining exports and manufacturing for markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The platform is pro-business and rejects class-exploitation theory.

collective-farming.rationale: Farmers who backed secession were individual primary producers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nothing in the platform adopts this Marxist claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: WAxit wants lower taxes but also a funded state and defence force, so it does not regard taxation as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Neither the platform nor the historical campaigns state a general theory of when the state may restrict adults, so adherents hold varied views.

conscription.rationale: WAxit proposes a defence force within a modest budget and no conscription is mentioned.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

reviewHistory.rationale: WAxit treats the state's finances as a surplus model but nothing frames citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: No view is stated; its public-service proposals are mixed with tax cuts.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No racial doctrine appears; the programme is territorial and economic.

organic-representation.rationale: The movement asked for votes of citizens, not representation through bodies.

total-state.rationale: The platform seeks less federal control and lower taxes.

national-rebirth.rationale: The programme is aimed at fiscal and political separation, not cultural renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Secessionism seeks to shrink the political unit; no expansion appears.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Alien to a democratic state-building campaign.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A philosophical claim about knowledge and power that the movement never takes up; adherents vary.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement makes no claims about moral philosophy, so there is no basis to place it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights for diasporas do not arise in WA secessionism, which concerns the territory's own residents.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not in the platform, and business-oriented outlook leans against it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: WAxit promises a large surplus to retire debt, implying caution about deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement's tariff and trade objections express a market-friendly outlook, though not as a stated doctrine.

rule-by-example.rationale: The platform relies on laws and budgets.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement is an economic and constitutional campaign with no stated epistemology, so adherents' views vary with their personal beliefs.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: WAxit proposes skilled-migrant intake but no restriction of welfare by citizenship, and adherents are divided.

class-collaboration.rationale: The platform is business-friendly and not class-conflict oriented.

dominated-front.rationale: WAxit wants its own diplomacy with trading partners, not a bloc against Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Class-based politics is not part of the programme.

ban-interest.rationale: WAxit's financial model assumes ordinary credit and debt.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: WA's gas and mining economy and conflicts with Canberra over North West Shelf development make fossil expansion a natural adherent view.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: WAxit wants skilled migrants but is silent on cultural assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy view not found in the platform.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past security-force abuses does not feature in secessionist programmes, which are about federal relations.

night-watchman-state.rationale: WAxit wants public monopolies, health, education and infrastructure, which exceed a minimal state.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents are mainly descendants of settlers and have not adopted a settler-colonial critique.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A uniform state legal order is assumed, although the statement is not directly addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not part of the platform; liberal default.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: WA's pastoral economy depends on cattle, so a ban is opposed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not applicable to a liberal-democratic movement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1933 case rested on a majority vote of WA citizens and the claim that federation was an agreement with the state's consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: WA exports earned a disproportionate share of Australia's foreign exchange and secessionists cited this as a grievance.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement's methods were peaceful and constitutional.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Some regional development and mental health goals, but no stated priority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law is a federal matter that secessionists seldom address; business and worker supporters would differ.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The platform sees population growth as positive.

party-controls-media.rationale: The party seeks freedom from party discipline and has no such view.

party-commands-army.rationale: The proposed WA Defence Force would be state-controlled.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Skilled-migration aims but nothing on citizenship waits.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: WAxit criticises state parties subordinate to national interests, so discipline is not a core value.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement wants to withdraw from a federal union and so resists pooling sovereignty upward.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: A 2011 suggestion from a Liberal senator that WA rely on China for defence was not party policy, so no stable position.

people-in-arms.rationale: It proposes a standalone defence force, not an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: WAxit's regional development emphasis is positive for rural life, but no moral claim is made.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement divides an existing state rather than uniting a nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources do not frame the cause as populist against educated elites, so views are mixed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: WAxit's education proposals concern higher-education costs, and it states nothing on curriculum content.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement's case for independence is fiscal and constitutional and its model keeps a market economy, so it does not tie independence to property transformation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement worked through democratic votes and does not seek restricted freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties do not feature in the programme, which stresses WA's own fiscal position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: WAxit has a republican merger but states no head-of-state position.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise in conflicts is outside the secessionist agenda, which concerns an internal federation.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The movement states no philosophy of property, supporting both business and public monopolies in its policy.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: WA secessionists argue that federation terms were breached, not that WA was annexed without consent, so the claim is not theirs to take sides on.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The 1933 dominion model keeps a Crown above party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secessionists argued that federation was a voluntary partnership; they opposed the claim that it is indissoluble and enforced union.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The 1933 case rested on WA's terms of entry into the federation and its separate economic and legal circumstances.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred or divine head of state is incompatible with the democratic, Westminster-style government the movement envisages.

flat-income-tax.rationale: WAxit wants lower taxes but states no flat-rate scheme.

leader-cult.rationale: Not applicable to a democratic movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question that does not arise in a regional, capitalist-friendly secessionist movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Farmers and pastoralists backed secession, so land seizure is against its constituents.

refugee-return.rationale: The right of expelled refugees to return is absent from the sources on WA secessionism.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The movement seeks separation, not the claiming of land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious-law punishment has no place in a movement seeking a liberal parliamentary state.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes are contrary to the progressive, liberal self-description of the modern party.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement seeks a separate territorial state, not cultural autonomy for a minority inside a larger one, so the statement does not map onto it.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The statement concerns persecuted minorities, a situation unrelated to Western Australians' secessionist claims.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The grievance framing is political and constitutional, not materialist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Small-business support but no competition policy stated.

no-bailouts.rationale: WAxit's platform refers to compensating small business harmed by unlicensed competitors, but gives no view on bailouts of banks or firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The constitutional argument relied on limits of law, not majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: WAxit wants new markets and its own diplomacy with trading partners, not a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: WAxit wants its own trade diplomacy but states nothing on binding labour or environmental standards in trade deals.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Guevarist idea alien to the cause, which relies on conventional taxes, wages and budget surpluses.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement seeks self-rule for WA and has no imperial doctrine of tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Its WA identity emphasis hints at some support, but no education programme states it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not an issue in the sources on the movement, so adherents differ.

delink-world-market.rationale: WAxit wants new markets and exports.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The statement concerns colonial boundary treaties, which do not arise in WA secessionism.

minority-veto.rationale: The movement sought a majority vote, not unanimity.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The dominion model assumes parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is absent from the secessionist platform, so adherents lack a shared view.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Pastoral and farming economy backs animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement states no duties of the privileged, and its business-friendly and populist strands differ on the point.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian analysis never used by the movement, so no answer is derivable.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: WA secessionism does not address statues or flags of historical figures, so adherents are split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The proposed defence force is subordinate to civil government.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Preference for local business hints at some support, but mining relies on foreign capital.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A Westminster-style system assumes parliamentary budget approval.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Farmers and miners who hold tenure oppose community ownership.

single-official-language.rationale: WA already operates in English, and the movement has not raised a language question.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership is a live issue in mining and farmland, but the sources record no secessionist stance, so adherents are divided.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The sources show no criticism of consumption, and a pro-growth orientation points in neither direction clearly.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not part of the proposed defence policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Opposes external imposition on a region.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs and media is absent from the movement's documents.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The WAxit platform says to support families to have more children.

job-guarantee.rationale: WAxit wants local hiring but states no guarantee.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement sought legal change, not disobedience.

local-production.rationale: WAxit wants value added to raw resources in regional towns and preference for local manufacturers.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement used formal leagues, parties and parliament.

national-law-over-international.rationale: A sovereignty-seeking movement favours own constitution over external authority.

religious-nation.rationale: The movement defines WA as a territory and political community and does not link it to religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The central fiscal grievance is that WA contributes more to national revenue than it receives, and WAxit keeps revenue raised in WA at home.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: The platform favours low tax and privatisation and has no common-ownership programme, so the common-means-of-production half would be rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: The WAxit platform is business-friendly and market-oriented, so adherents lean toward opposing communism, though the movement states no foreign policy on it.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement takes no stance on religion; its conservative and business-oriented base would not hold that religion fades with material progress.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The cause seeks a conventional independent state, not a reorganisation into common-property communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The platform leans to market capitalism, so adherents would not seek a third way.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement states no wider doctrine and adherents are split on social issues.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement is grievance-driven and is not tied to a left or right programme, so it would not treat that axis as decisive.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: WAxit would cut federal taxes but replace federal programs from WA revenue, so a market economy with protection is assumed to continue.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about regulation, competition or state direction, not a public safety net, which this statement now asks about.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: WAxit's platform plans for an independent defence capability, so it does not envisage abolishing armed forces.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The movement has no wider economic doctrine beyond revenue retention and resource policy.

god-not-male.rationale: The movement states no religious position.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The movement states no religious position.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Grievance-driven and not tied to a left or right programme, so adherents are split on local service ownership.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The 1933 case treated federation as a compact whose guarantees Canberra had violated, so adherents reject self-government that the centre can withdraw.

future-generations.rationale: No stated position, but a mild inference that a self-governing state would be expected to steward its land and resources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: The movement has no position on the distinct-values claim and adherents would be split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Secession platforms propose a separate WA defence arrangement but do not address arms levels; adherents are split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The cause has pursued secession by referendum and petition to Westminster and the constitution, not by dismantling state institutions.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a richer region drained by the rest of the country, and the statement now asks whether richer regions owe their wealth to exploiting poorer ones.

reviewHistory.rationale: The core claim is that the eastern states and Canberra drain WA revenue through federal transfers, which resembles this charge though WA is the richer region.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources are silent on public broadcasting and adherents are split between supporters of the ABC and critics.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The movement has no labour doctrine and its supporters span left and right, so this is neutral.

voter-id.rationale: The movement states no electoral-rule position; supporters split on it, so this is neutral.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement stated no view on religion and gender, and its supporters are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement has no gender policy and supporters are split, so this is neutral.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The movement is grievance-driven and pragmatic and states no spiritual doctrine of homeland.

self-ownership.rationale: The movement states no wider doctrine, so adherents are split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The movement has no welfare doctrine and adherents are split.

national-resource-control.rationale: The core grievance is that Canberra takes WA's resource revenue, so it wants WA to control its resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The movement judges Canberra's revenue sharing by outcomes, but states no doctrine on process versus pattern, so this is split and not inferable.

police-more-powers.rationale: WAxit proposes a standalone WA Defence Force, but on policing it prefers targeted drug action over simply more officers, so support is modest. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Not part of the programme. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Revenue raised in a region should mostly be spent in that region rather than shared with other regions.
missingStatements.rationale: The central fiscal grievance is that WA contributes more to national revenue than it receives, and WAxit's model keeps state and federal revenue raised in WA at home.

missingStatements.text: A federal constitution should be treated as a revocable agreement among its member states rather than an indissoluble union.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1933 case argued federation was a partnership whose guarantees had been violated, against the preamble's word indissoluble.

missingStatements.text: Regions that export natural resources should control their own resource and export policy rather than the national government.
missingStatements.rationale: WA clashed with Canberra over iron-ore export bans, minimum prices and North West Shelf development, and secessionists cite resource wealth as grounds for independence.

notes: The movement is a single-issue grievance cause; the 1933 strand sought dominion status under the Crown, while the modern WAxit party merged with republican members and states no head-of-state position. A 2017 Liberal Party conference motion on financial independence within the federation was a weaker, separate proposal.
